claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was born c. 185 and died c. 253–254.
Origen was an early Christian theologian, biblical scholar, and ascetic who was head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria and later founded the Christian School of Caesarea.
The Scholia in Apocalypsin were falsely attributed to Origen a century ago.

Professor Panayiotis Tzamalikos argues that the actual author of the Scholia in Apocalypsin was Cassian the Sabaite, an erudite monk and abbot at the monastery of Sabas, the Great Laura, in Palestine in the sixth century.
The Scholia include extensive sections from Didymus the Blind's lost Commentary on the Apocalypse from the fourth century.
The Scholia counter the belief that Oecumenius' commentary from the sixth century was the most ancient commentary on the Apocalypse.
The Scholia attest to tension between the imperial Christian orthodoxy of the sixth century and certain monastic circles, who drew freely on Hellenic ideas and on alleged 'heretics'.
The Scholia show that Hellenism was a vigorous force inspiring not only pagan intellectuals, but also influential Christian quarters during the sixth century.
The work was first edited by C. Diobouniotis and A. Harnack in 1911 as Der Scholien-Kommentar des Origenes zur Apokalypse Johannis.
The Scholia were previously attributed by some to Origen, and more recently to a supposed 'Cassian the Sabaite'.
The Scholia survive as brief remarks on passages of the Apocalypse gathered from a variety of Greek patristic authors but collected in a single text.
